Maybe a possible explanation could be the added lightmap data from static objects. If that is the case it would probably be more of a unity issue. The more surface area, the more the lightmapper has to cover.. and all of that data is a huge bitmap essentially
Have you tried messing with your lightmap compress settings at all? That could further reduce your mb's. Good luck & I hope you find out exactly what it was!
@{5ea7811b606e142075eeced2|full_name}: Actually what was causing it was having the objects set to static batching. For some reason this is currently bugged in unity and eats a lot of information.

details:
EDIT: I figured out the issue with the file size, it ended up being the way I was setting plants as static and unity just not liking it.

Original post:

Okay, so I decided to start using the SDK3 for making new worlds and decided to start with a simple home world. I made the place kind of big with lots of trees and plants and a house. The file size ended up a pretty standard 200 something MB. Performance wasn't great so I went back in and made the world smaller. The world had less stuff in it over all, but when I went to check it out, the performance was even worse and the file size had tripled to a whopping *600 MB.* I thought maybe I was putting to many trees in, so I made it even smaller, with far less objects in it. After uploading it the file size was now nearly 1,000 MB!! I didn't bother letting it load in. 
At this point I went and looked in the bug reports and some people were saying that Udon SDK3 scans all objects in the project at run time, and I wondered if that was the cause of the issue. So I decided to clean out anything I wasn't using from the project files in hopes of making it small again. This didn't really do anything as it stayed around the same file size even after crunching more textures.
So this time I decided to drastically reduce the amount of light probes by nearly half and I cleared out the dynamic objects and dynamic materials again because they had reset themselves. I rebaked the lightmaps and double checked I didn't have anything hidden in the map. This time I didn't even bother with a play test in Unity. Despite my best efforts, this only reduced the file size by about 9 MB, bringing it to a total of **939 MB.** My world is only a 200x200 terrain piece with a house. It shouldn't be this big. 
As a last resort, I uploaded the world again with a new blueprint ID, deleting the old version. This only reduced it to 918 MB. Once again I decided to reduce the amount of light probes. I rebaked the lighting. The file size stayed the same. At this point I have no idea what is causing the file size issues except maybe the SDK is uploading everything in the project and maybe more stuff that I'm not aware of, like maybe the GI cache?
TLDR: File size is like 10 times bigger than it should be and there's almost no way to reduce it.
title: [fixed] Udon Worlds are a HUGE file size!
